title: Maximum Sum of Subsequence With Non-adjacent Elements
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` and a list `queries`, where `queries[i] = [pos_i, x_i]`. Handle the queries in order. Query `i` first overwrites `nums[pos_i]` with `x_i` (the change stays in place for later queries), and its answer is then the largest total you can get by picking elements of `nums` so that no two picked elements sit at neighbouring indices. Picking nothing is allowed and totals 0.

Add up the answers of all the queries and return that total modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

Without updates this is the classic take-or-skip DP: walk the array tracking the best total that picks or skips the current element. Rerunning it after every update costs O(n · q), up to 2.5 · 10^9 steps. A segment tree recomputes only the O(log n) ranges that contain the changed position, provided two neighbouring ranges' summaries can be glued together.

Gluing a left range to the right range next to it has one conflict: the left range's last element and the right range's first element cannot both be picked. So each node keeps four best totals: `full` (no restriction), `skipFirst`, `skipLast` and `skipBoth` (those end elements left out). The glue decides which side of the seam stays out.

## Approach

1. A leaf with value `v` has `full = max(0, v)` (pick it or not); with its only element left out, every other field is 0.
2. `merge(left, right)` keeps the outer restriction and takes the better seam choice, e.g. `full = max(left.skipLast + right.full, left.full + right.skipFirst)`.
3. `build` fills the tree from `nums`, merging children bottom-up.
4. For each query, `update` replaces the leaf at `pos` and re-merges its ancestors; the root's `full` is that query's answer, added to `total` modulo `10^9 + 7`.

## Example 1, step by step

The root splits `nums` into `[3, 5]` and `[9]`. After the first query `nums = [3, -2, 9]`; the left part gets `full = skipLast = 3` (take the 3) and `skipFirst = skipBoth = 0`, so the root's `full = max(3 + 9, 3 + 0) = 12`. After the second query the 3 becomes -3, every field of the left part drops to 0, and the root's `full = max(0 + 9, 0 + 0) = 9`. So `total = 12 + 9 = 21`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + q log n): building visits each node once, and each update re-merges O(log n) nodes in O(1).
- Space: O(n) for the tree.

## Pitfalls

- The empty choice is allowed: a leaf's `full` is `max(0, v)`, so an all-negative array scores 0.
- Never add `left.full + right.full`: that may pick both neighbours at the seam.
- Updates persist: each query starts from the array the earlier ones left.
- Reduce `total` modulo `10^9 + 7` after every query.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tree` | node summaries, root at index 1, children at `2 * node` and `2 * node + 1` |
| `full`, `skipFirst`, `skipLast`, `skipBoth` | a range's best total with no restriction, or with that end element (or both) left out |
| `node`, `start`, `end`, `mid` | a tree node, the index range it covers, and the split point |
| `pos`, `x` / `value` | the query's position and its new value |
| `total` | the sum of the answers so far, modulo `10^9 + 7` |

narration.6: A segment tree over n positions needs at most 4n slots; the root sits at index 1.
narration.9: One element: with no restriction, take it only if it is positive; if it must stay out, the best is 0.
narration.15: No outer restriction: either the left part's last element stays out, or the right part's first element does.
narration.16: The same seam choice, with the left part's first element (the range's first) left out.
narration.17: The same seam choice, with the right part's last element (the range's last) left out.
narration.18: Both outer ends left out, plus the seam choice.
narration.23: A range of one index is a leaf.
narration.30: Glue the two halves into this node's summary.
narration.35: Replace its summary with the new value.
narration.39: Only the half that contains pos changes.
narration.44: Re-glue this node, since one of its children just changed.
narration.49: Handle the queries in order; each update stays for later ones.
narration.50: Overwrite nums[pos] with x, refreshing the O(log n) summaries above it.
narration.51: The root's unrestricted best is this query's answer; add it to the running total.
narration.53: Return the sum of all the answers, modulo 10^9 + 7.
